title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 237
paragraphs: To him Xerxes replied as follows: “Achaimenes, I think you speak well, and so I will do. But Demaratos is saying what he believes to be best for me, though his opinion is overruled by yours. For I will certainly not accept what you said — namely that he is not well-disposed to my cause — judging both by what he has said before now and by this truth: that though one fellow-citizen envies another's good fortune and shows hostility by silence, nor would one citizen, when consulted by a fellow-citizen, suggest the course that seemed best to him (unless he had attained a great height of virtue — and such men are few), yet guest-friend to guest-friend in prosperity is as well-disposed as anyone on earth, and if his friend consults him, he will give him the best advice. As for slander against Demaratos — who is my guest-friend — I bid everyone refrain from it in the future.”
